# Pre-Implementation Checklist: Document Ingestion Endpoint

**Purpose**: Formal pre-implementation gate — validate the quality, clarity, completeness, and
consistency of this feature's requirements (spec.md, plan.md, research.md, data-model.md,
contracts/) before `/speckit-tasks` breaks them into implementation work. This checks whether the
requirements are well-written, not whether any code works.
**Created**: 2026-08-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context
and requirements. All 32 items below were resolved on 2026-08-15 by amending spec.md, research.md,
plan.md, data-model.md, and contracts/ingestion-api-contract.md — see the resolution note under
each item for exactly what changed.

## Requirement Completeness (Ingestion Pipeline)

- [x] CHK001 Are the exact conditions for classifying an uploaded file's type (content-sniffed vs. declared `Content-Type` vs. filename extension) stated in FR-002 itself, or only inferred from the downstream API contract? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, Gap]
  - **Resolved**: FR-002 now states directly that type is "determined from the file's actual content, not merely a filename extension or a caller-declared content type."
- [x] CHK002 Is a requirement documented for how the pipeline behaves when a single document's extracted text would produce more chunks than the embedding provider's per-request batch limit allows? [Completeness, Gap] (research.md "Open questions")
  - **Resolved**: research.md Decision 4 now specifies a sub-batching loop (2048-input ceiling); FR-008 and a new Assumptions bullet in spec.md reference it explicitly.
- [x] CHK003 Is there a documented upper bound on end-to-end processing time for a near-maximum-size (20 MB) upload, beyond SC-001's "typical" multi-page target? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §SC-001]
  - **Resolved**: new **SC-006** — a maximum-size (20 MB) file resolves (success or failure) within 60 seconds.
- [x] CHK004 Are structured-logging requirements for each embedding request and database write (constitution "Error Handling & Logging") captured in any of this feature's requirement documents, or only deferred as an implementation-phase task in plan.md? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-014]
  - **Resolved**: new **FR-016** requires structured logging of every upload outcome, embedding request, and database write; plan.md's Constitution Check updated to cite it instead of deferring.
- [x] CHK005 Is a requirement defined for how the endpoint responds to a malformed multipart request (e.g., missing `file` part, missing filename, absent `Content-Disposition`)? [Completeness, Gap, Edge Case]
  - **Resolved**: new Edge Cases bullet + FR-003 extension covering no/duplicate `file` part and a `file` part with no filename → `invalid_file`.

## Requirement Clarity & Measurability

- [x] CHK006 Is "a typical multi-page policy document (a few pages of text)" in SC-001 quantified precisely enough (e.g., page count, token count) to be objectively measured against the 15-second target? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001]
  - **Resolved**: SC-001 now cites concrete figures (~7–8 pages, ~1,800 words) verified against the actual sample corpus (`security-policy.pdf`/`travel-expense-policy.pdf`).
- [x] CHK007 Is the 500–1000-token chunk-size bound in FR-006 written to acknowledge the documented exception for a document's final or sole chunk (research.md Decision 3), or could a reader of spec.md alone interpret it as an unconditional bound? [Clarity, Consistency, Spec §FR-006]
  - **Resolved**: FR-006 now states the final/sole-chunk exception directly, not only in research.md.
- [x] CHK008 Is the 20 MB maximum file size treated with the same testable rigor as a numbered functional requirement, or does its placement in Assumptions rather than the Functional Requirements list risk being overlooked during test planning? [Clarity, Traceability, Spec Assumptions]
  - **Resolved**: the number now lives in **FR-003** itself; the Assumptions entry is rationale-only and points back to FR-003 as the source of truth.
- [x] CHK009 Can SC-005's "no data from one [document] affecting the other" be objectively verified as written, or does it need decomposition into specific measurable checks (e.g., independent identifiers, independent deletion)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
  - **Resolved**: SC-005 decomposed into three specific checks (distinct identifiers, independently complete chunk sets, independent deletion).
- [x] CHK010 Is FR-014's "MUST NOT include credentials... in any log output or error response" paired with a concrete, verifiable check (what to inspect, what constitutes a pass), or does it state intent without a verification method? [Measurability, Spec §FR-014]
  - **Resolved**: FR-014 now states the verification method directly (grep log/response output for the key value; review every log/error code path) and what MAY vs MUST NOT be logged.

## Requirement Consistency (Spec ↔ Plan/Research/Contract)

- [x] CHK011 Is "AI provider unconfigured" (contracts/ingestion-api-contract.md's `provider_unconfigured` code) explicitly classified under one of FR-011's two named failure categories within spec.md itself, or does that classification exist only in the Phase 1 contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011]
  - **Resolved**: FR-011 rewritten to explicitly group "provider unconfigured" under the "processing failed" category, with rationale.
- [x] CHK012 Does FR-009's "full set of chunks" language read unambiguously for the zero-chunk case FR-015 permits, or could "full set" be misread as implying at least one chunk? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009 vs §FR-015]
  - **Resolved**: FR-009 now states explicitly that "full set" includes the empty set, cross-referencing FR-015.
- [x] CHK013 Is the Assumptions section's "single file per request" interpretation of the constitution's plural "MUST accept .txt and .pdf uploads" phrasing explicitly justified as a scope decision, or could it read as an unconfirmed narrowing of a constitutional requirement? [Consistency, Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
  - **Resolved**: Assumptions bullet rewritten to state and justify this reading explicitly, rather than silently assuming it.
- [x] CHK014 Are the error-code names in contracts/ingestion-api-contract.md (`unsupported_type`, `invalid_file`, `unparseable`, `provider_unconfigured`, `processing_failed`) each traceable to a specific FR, or do any exist only at the contract layer with no corresponding spec-level requirement? [Traceability, Consistency]
  - **Resolved**: all five now trace to spec.md (FR-002/003/005 directly; `provider_unconfigured`/`processing_failed` via FR-011's rewritten categorization).

## API Contract Completeness (`POST /documents`)

- [x] CHK015 Is the behavior specified for a multipart request containing the `file` part plus additional, unexpected form fields (ignored vs. rejected)? [Completeness, Gap, Contract]
  - **Resolved**: contract now states extra fields are ignored, not rejected, with rationale (forward compatibility).
- [x] CHK016 Is the response behavior specified for a request whose `file` part is present but carries no `filename` at all? [Completeness, Gap, Edge Case]
  - **Resolved**: covered by the same FR-003/Edge Cases update as CHK005 — `invalid_file`.
- [x] CHK017 Are response header requirements (e.g., `Content-Type: application/json`) stated consistently for both success and every error status code, not just the success example? [Completeness, Contract]
  - **Resolved**: contract now states `Content-Type: application/json` applies to every response, success or error, with no exception.
- [x] CHK018 Is it specified whether concurrent identical uploads (same file content, submitted at the same instant) are both guaranteed to succeed independently, or could a race condition around filename/content be interpreted as needing dedup? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec Edge Cases]
  - **Resolved**: Edge Cases bullet extended to explicitly cover byte-identical concurrent uploads — no deduplication, two ordinary independent requests.

## Security & Data Handling

- [x] CHK019 Are the file-size and file-type validation checks (FR-002, FR-003) explicitly ordered relative to each other (i.e., which rejection applies when a file is both oversized and an unsupported type)? [Clarity, Gap]
  - **Resolved**: FR-003 and Edge Cases now state the order explicitly (size before type), and the contract adds a "Validation order" note.
- [x] CHK020 Is a requirement defined for whether the original filename is sanitized/validated before being stored or echoed back in a response (e.g., path-traversal characters, control characters)? [Completeness, Gap, Security]
  - **Resolved**: new **FR-017** — filename is stored verbatim as opaque text, never interpreted as a path or executed; Assumptions explains why no further sanitization is needed.
- [x] CHK021 Beyond "no credentials in logs," are there requirements distinguishing what MAY be logged about a rejected or failed upload (e.g., filename, size, error code) from what MUST NOT be (e.g., raw file content)? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-014]
  - **Resolved**: covered by the same FR-014 rewrite as CHK010 — explicit MAY/MUST NOT log-content lists.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for a client disconnecting or the request timing out mid-upload, before the pipeline completes? [Coverage, Gap, Exception Flow]
  - **Resolved**: new Edge Cases bullet — treated as an ordinary mid-pipeline failure under FR-009, retry behaves as a new upload.
- [x] CHK023 Is the "unusual character encoding" edge case (garbled `.txt` text) paired with a concrete detection criterion an implementer could test against, or does it rely on Tika's default behavior being assumed correct without a stated requirement? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases]
  - **Resolved**: Edge Cases bullet rewritten with a concrete criterion (undecodable as valid text → treated as parse failure, `unparseable`) and an explicit "MUST NOT guess or transliterate" rule.
- [x] CHK024 Are recovery/retry requirements consistent between the general FR-011 guidance and the specific per-error-code retry guidance table in contracts/ingestion-api-contract.md? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011]
  - **Resolved**: verified consistent — FR-011's rewritten two-category split matches the contract's `4xx`/`503` table and Decision 8 exactly; no change needed to the contract's table itself.
- [x] CHK025 Is the "divider page with no extractable text" edge case's expected chunk/page-number behavior specified precisely enough to be tested (e.g., does the page still count toward page numbering for subsequent pages)? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases]
  - **Resolved**: bullet extended — page numbering is always the true 1-indexed source position, never renumbered around skipped pages.

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK026 Are throughput/concurrency expectations quantified (e.g., how many simultaneous uploads the system is expected to handle without degradation), or only qualitatively described as "independently processed"? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases]
  - **Resolved**: new Assumptions bullet states explicitly that no concurrency ceiling is defined and why (PoC usage pattern), rather than leaving it silently unaddressed.
- [x] CHK027 Is a requirement defined for observable/queryable ingestion status (e.g., can an operator tell how many documents have been ingested, or must this be inferred by querying the database directly)? [Completeness, Gap]
  - **Resolved**: new Assumptions text states this is explicitly out of scope (query the database directly, or a future admin feature) and clarifies FR-016's logging is diagnostic, not a status API.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK028 Is the dependency on feature 003's `documents`/`chunks` schema contracts remaining unchanged (no column additions) explicitly re-validated as a precondition before this feature's implementation begins? [Dependency, Traceability, Spec Key Entities]
  - **Resolved**: spec.md's Key Entities section now states this as an explicit implementation precondition; quickstart.md's Prerequisites adds a concrete `psql` check for it.
- [x] CHK029 Is the assumption that Azure OpenAI's embedding API accepts a full document's chunk set as one batched request validated against that API's actual documented limits, or is it currently an unverified assumption carried from research.md alone? [Assumption, research.md Decision 4]
  - **Resolved**: research.md Decision 4 now cites the documented 2048-input-per-request ceiling and handles it via a sub-batching loop rather than assuming it away.
- [x] CHK030 Is the "no authentication/authorization" assumption cross-checked against whether any other in-repo requirement (constitution or prior spec) implies an upload-time actor identity is needed for a future feature (e.g., audit trail)? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
  - **Resolved**: Assumptions bullet extended to state explicitly that no other spec/constitution section in the repo currently implies an audit-trail requirement.

## Ambiguities, Gaps & Conflicts Needing Resolution

- [x] CHK031 Does the spec resolve whether `processing_failed` (embedding/DB failure) and `provider_unconfigured` should be surfaced to the caller as distinguishable error codes, given both map to `503` but arise from meaningfully different causes for an operator to act on? [Ambiguity, Contract]
  - **Resolved**: contract now states the rationale explicitly — two distinct `error` codes sharing one status code, so a status-code-only caller and a code-reading operator both get correct behavior.
- [x] CHK032 Is there a single, agreed source of truth for the maximum accepted file size (spec.md Assumptions states 20 MB) that a future consumer (e.g., the eventual frontend upload view) is required to reference rather than restate independently? [Consistency, Assumption]
  - **Resolved**: FR-003 is now the stated single source of truth; the contract, data-model.md, and Assumptions all reference it instead of independently asserting the number.
